title: Find the loops
description:
A disassembler has listed every jump in a function: each one has the address it is at and the address it jumps to. A jump whose target is at or before its own address is a **back edge**, and its target is the head of a loop.

Write `loopHeads(jumps)`, which returns the distinct loop-head addresses, sorted ascending, together with, for each head, how many back edges lead to it (a loop with `continue` statements can have several).

```
jumps:  0x1010 -> 0x1040   (forward: an if)
        0x1030 -> 0x1018   (back edge)
        0x1050 -> 0x1018   (back edge to the same head)
        0x1060 -> 0x1060   (a jump to itself: an infinite loop of one instruction)
result: { 0x1018, 2 }, { 0x1060, 1 }
```
hints: A back edge is any jump with `to <= from`. Count them per target in a `std::map`, which also keeps the targets sorted.
A `std::vector` of pairs can be built directly from a map's begin and end iterators.
